title: Dynamic counterparty profile and auto-redline suggestions for MSA/DPA
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a lightweight service and UI layer that generates a dynamic counterparty risk profile from SSQ metadata, usage telemetry, and previous negotiation history, then surface automated redline suggestions for common MSA/DPA clauses (indemnity, liability caps, data residency, escrow). The feature should enable sales to get a preclearance score and suggested clause edits in under 2 minutes, and produce an evidence checklist to accelerate legal review. This reduces manual triage, shortens negotiation cycles, and aligns pricing/commitments with contract risk.
goals: Reduce average time-to-first-redline for enterprise deals from 3 business days to <4 hours
Decrease legal queue volume for low-risk SSQs by 40% through automated auto-approve suggestions
Provide sales with an actionable preclearance score and suggested pricing adjustments linked to indemnity/liability changes
success_metrics: Median time from contract intake to first suggested redline <= 4 hours
% of SSQs receiving automated suggestions: target 60% for Tier A/B customers
Reduction in legal manual reviews for auto-approved items by 40% within quarter
scope_in: Data ingest pipeline for SSQ metadata and contract history
Risk heuristic service that returns a counterparty profile (risk bands) and suggested clause edits
Sales UI component in Contract Intake to display preclearance score, suggested redlines, and evidence checklist
Telemetry & audit log to track suggestion acceptance, overrides, and legal review outcomes
scope_out: Full automated legal sign-off for high-risk exceptions (still requires legal approval)
Automated re-pricing engine tied to billing (this will be a later integration)
On-prem/private deployment packaging for the v1 of the heuristic service
requirements: Define a minimal counterparty profile schema (risk_band, previous_exceptions_count, sensitive_data_flag, revenue_tier, geographic_fragments)
Map common redline-able clauses to parameterized templates (indemnity, liability cap, escrow, data residency, termination)
Frontend Contract Intake card with 'Get preclearance' CTA and a results panel with accept/reject for each suggested clause
Tracking events: suggestion_generated, suggestion_accepted, suggestion_rejected, legal_override, final_decision
Legal playbook documents that explain heuristic rules and override guidance for reviewers
acceptance_criteria: Given an SSQ for a customer with no prior exceptions, the heuristic service produces a preclearance score and at least one suggested clause or 'no change' within 2 minutes
Sales UI displays the evidence checklist and allows sales to attach contextual notes before routing to legal
Telemetry shows suggestion_accepted or suggestion_rejected events with user id and timestamp
Legal can view the generated risk profile and accept/override suggestions; overrides are recorded and used to tune heuristics
Automated suggestions do not propose changes that increase legal exposure beyond existing internal guardrails (guardrails documented in legal playbook)
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature flagged internal alpha for Solutions Engineering + Legal (limited to 25 deals)
Week 3: Expand flag to Sales Ops pilot (50 deals) and capture telemetry
Week 6: Gradual rollout to self-serve enterprise intake + training docs for AMs
Post-rollout: 8-week tuning window where legal-curated overrides update heuristic weights
tasks: Define counterparty profile spec with Legal and RevOps
Prototype heuristic ruleset and mapping to clause templates (PM + Legal)
Build Contract Intake UI card and backend API (Frontend + Backend)
Run 2-week internal alpha and collect feedback
Tune heuristics based on overrides and produce a public playbook
open_questions: What is the minimum set of SSQ fields required to produce a reliable preclearance score?
Do we allow Sales to accept suggestions without legal review for 'auto-approve' low-risk band? If so, what guardrails?
Should the heuristic include usage telemetry (past 30-day token consumption) to influence indemnity exposure?
Where will the evidence artifacts be stored (Confluence link vs. customer record in CRM)?
decisions: Heuristic will be conservative by default and only mark 'auto-approve' when risk_band == 'low' and previous_exceptions_count == 0
Suggested clause edits will be parameterized templates (text snippets) that legal can approve to become canonical
Telemetry will be retained for 12 months and surfaced to Legal dashboards for tuning
notes: This ticket combines product + legal + revops effort; early alignment with Legal on guardrails is critical
We aim to avoid proposing increases to indemnity or higher liability exposure than baseline; suggestions should only reduce exposure or propose equivalent tradeoffs
Design should make it obvious when a suggestion is machine-generated vs. legal-generated to preserve reviewer trust
